levels.title: Fresh
levels.summary: Looking for your first iOS job.
levels.description: You know Swift basics and have built small apps to learn. You have not worked as an iOS developer yet, or only as an intern.
selfCheck: I can write Swift code with variables, functions, optionals and collections.
I can build a simple app with a few screens in SwiftUI or UIKit.
I can explain the difference between a struct and a class.
I can use Git to save and share my code.
I can solve easy coding problems in Swift.

levels.title: Junior
levels.summary: You build features on a team, with help.
levels.description: You work on an iOS team and finish tasks and small projects with guidance. You can fix bugs in code that other people wrote.
selfCheck: I can load data from a web API and show it in a list.
I can explain how ARC works and find a retain cycle.
I can use delegates, closures and notifications, and say when to use each.
I can save data on the device.
I can find the cause of a crash with Xcode.
I can write basic unit tests.

levels.title: Mid
levels.summary: You own features from start to end.
levels.description: You plan and build features with little help. You make technical choices for your features and help newer developers.
selfCheck: I can use async/await, tasks and actors, and explain Sendable.
I can compare app architectures like MVVM and choose one for a feature.
I can build a feature that is easy to test, using dependency injection.
I can find and fix common performance problems.
I can review other people's code and give useful feedback.
I can solve medium coding problems in Swift.

levels.title: Senior
levels.summary: You design systems and lead projects.
levels.description: You design the systems in your area and lead projects that affect other teams. You set the quality bar with reviews and mentoring.
selfCheck: I can design a full mobile feature: data, network, offline, caching and errors.
I can split a large app into modules with Swift packages.
I can find memory and speed problems with Instruments.
I can plan safe releases with feature flags, monitoring and crash reports.
I can mentor developers and lead technical decisions.
I can explain trade-offs to engineers and to people who do not code.

levels.title: Staff
levels.summary: You set technical direction for many teams.
levels.description: You plan the technical direction for many teams over years. You decide what to build, not only how. You connect technical work to business goals.
selfCheck: I can make a technical plan for the mobile platform for the next years.
I can decide when to build a tool and when to buy or reuse one.
I can design systems that many teams use and that are hard to use wrongly.
I can lead through influence, without being the manager.
I can handle disagreement and explain decisions to leaders.
